name: NVD (National Vulnerability Database)
gives: CVE records with CVSS, CPE, CWE; CVE API 2.0

why.quote: The NVD API is intended to be used to develop a service or services to search, display, analyze, retrieve, view and otherwise "get" information from NVD data.
why.basis: NVD API Terms of Use (script-rendered page: text read from the strings in NVD's page bundle); notice to show: "This product uses the NVD API but is not endorsed or certified by the NVD."; rate limits from https://nvd.nist.gov/developers/start-here: 5 requests in a rolling 30 seconds without a key

interface: CVE API 2.0 (https://services.nvd.nist.gov/rest/json/cves/2.0), answered 200 with lastModStartDate/lastModEndDate and pubStartDate/pubEndDate windows, 2000 a page; no key (public rate limit: 5 requests in a rolling 30 seconds).
notes: Allows our use (a news site showing derived aggregates and per-CVE identifiers) with NVD's notice shown; modified content may not be attributed to the NVD, so our totals are labelled ours. NIST gives no warranty on the data. CVE records are not personal data. Aggregate-only on cyber.promptugal.news.
how: Every 6 hours, up to four GETs of the CVE API with no key and 7 seconds apart: one window of CVEs modified since 00:00 UTC yesterday (pages of 2000; the new CVEs are those published in the same window) (sources/nvd-cve/collect.mjs); keeps id, dates, status, CNA, CVSS severity and score, CWE ids, vendor and product, and whole-day totals (daily_totals, 30 days); no descriptions or references; served at /api/v1/nvd-cve/; raw kept in the vault copy. Asked by cyber.b@PrompTugal.dinis, 18 Nov 2026.
readers: sources/nvd-cve (every 6 hours: CVEs modified since 00:00 UTC yesterday)
sources/nvd-kev (daily since 19 Nov 2026 02:17 UTC: hasKev, every CVE on CISA KEV, one request; asked by cyber.b@)
review_note: nvd-kev ran first on 19 Nov 2026 02:17 UTC under the same terms and limits as nvd-cve (no key, 7 seconds apart, no descriptions or references kept); to be reviewed by security@ at its next sweep (conductor.b@ relayed, 02:22 UTC). No date-range gap reader exists; none is built until security@ clears it.
